findings.reason: The construction/conditional-input gap at ML.4 is real, with a narrower repair than the proposed blanket classification roadmap. ET.3 explicitly excludes the general weighted fundamental lemma, ET.6 constructs GL_m and its inner forms, and ET.7's unitary weak transfer does not construct all classical-group packets. The accepted BCGP21 route 4 proposal GSp4LocalLanglandsAndGaloisRepresentations does exist, but its Scope and Joined proposal paragraphs expressly IMPORT Gan–Takeda, Definition 2.3.1 and Arthur's transfer/multiplicities from ML.4; its title is not a construction of that input. Route 8 confirms this division. Give those inputs explicit proof tasks under ML.4 or one coalesced classification continuation, preserving that proposal's existing local representation/Galois/archimedean ownership. Separate unconditional Gan–Takeda (Annals 173, Main Theorem pp. 1842–1843) from source-dependent global multiplicity assumptions. AGIKMS 2410.13504v3 pp. 5,15 supplies previously missing local intertwining results but still retains the twisted weighted fundamental lemma; neither ET.3 nor a weak generic transfer discharges it. Retain exact group, inner form, genericity and parameter restrictions for Gan–Ichino, Xu and real packets. The evidence enumerates nine papers, not eight; RS-21 is unreviewed and is not proof of live ownership. See the report for boundaries and acceptance gates.

The central premise that all six ML stages are mere registries is false. ML.2 explicitly says to supply the final potential-automorphy theorem, independently of infrastructure; ML.3 owns source-scoped symmetric-power automorphy and its analytic consequences. PA.5 supplies compatible-system transport and expressly leaves lifting to its dedicated owner. Moving all ML.2 mathematics there would violate this boundary. Current route-by-route recount gives 100 distinct missing items on 21 accepted source routes from 19 papers; the claimed 101 includes the rejected Beuzart-Plessis–Chaudouard25 route 8. Newton–Thorne26 accepted route 2 keeps endpoints in ML.3 while routes 5,15,16,17 give its proof methods named Part II suppliers. BCGET25 accepted route 1 explicitly places the Bianchi definitions, Ramanujan/Hecke bounds and mass-equidistribution application with ML.0/2/3; a missing word in coarse atlas descriptions does not erase that accepted construction brief. Its Theorems E–G (public version pp. 9–11) are applications with real additional hypotheses, not grounds for duplicating them in a p-adic-L-function roadmap. Finding 1 independently identifies the actual ML.4 ownership gap. This rejection does not certify closure of all 100 items or promote any pending proposal.

The no-owner claim misses the integrated reviewed fine node AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights:R15.4/edixhoven-weight-k-rho-and-its-comparison-with-serre-k. It explicitly assigns the proof of Edixhoven Theorem 4.5 to R20.3, identifies Gross's companion-form input in proof steps 4 and 6, and records the Coleman–Voloch p>2 removal of the exceptional hypothesis. Thus the non-exceptional companion/weight-optimisation proof already has a named owner; it must be expanded there, not invented as an unowned theorem. Only BCG25 route 6 and CG20 route 27 are accepted: IKM24 route 8 was rejected, explicitly retaining the exact exceptional-hypothesis/supplier gate. The proposed repair is mathematically wrong about Coleman–Voloch treating p=2,3: their public Theorem 0.1 assumes 2<k<=p and Corollary 0.2 assumes p>2; the introduction leaves the exceptional k=p=2 case open and warns that tame need not mean split in the exceptional case. Gross Prop. 13.8/Thm. 13.10/Cor. 13.11 (pp. 497–498) distinguishes the split ordinary companion theorem and the weight-one boundary. Do not conflate complementary weights, unramifiedness and the Frobenius-polynomial theorem, or treat IKM's unresolved route as accepted. This is not a certification of the outstanding exceptional-case proof.

DLB17 accepted route 5 sends exactly 26 missing items into R31.1/2/4. The current R31.1 restricts the specialization to curves and R31.4 specifies Emerton's degree-one promodular GL2/Q theorem; neither states the definite degree-zero branch. CC.8 supplies a generic topological adapter, not its Banach local–global theorem. Dospinescu–Le Bras 1509.00606v2 §4.1 pp. 20–22 constructs B-bar/Q split at p and ramified at infinity, X as the inverse limit of finite adelic double quotients and C^0(X); §5.1 pp. 25–26 defines the Hecke algebra/completion and assumes the LOCAL residual representation at p absolutely irreducible. Theorem 5.4 gives C^0(X)[mathfrak p] ≅ Pi(mathfrak p)^{⊕r}, r>0, for every maximal ideal of A[1/p]. Appendix §13 pp. 69–73 proves this via finite generation, dense crystalline points, Proposition 13.5 and the completed evaluation isomorphism. Add the explicit definite specialization and compatibility branch inside R31, importing generic CC, finite-level quaternionic/Jacquet–Langlands inputs and R30.5's family correspondence. Prove the comparison with degree-zero completed cohomology; do not duplicate its carrier or import the curve theorem by analogy. B-bar is still over Q, so the summary's other-number-fields warning is not the reason the claim holds.
